packs.title: Action thriller
packs.summary: Engine: set-piece survival under a clock; chase geography and physical competence drive the page; emotional stakes hitch to each ordeal so spectacle isn’t empty.

packs.title: Adventure (commercial quest / journey)
packs.summary: Engine: leave the familiar world, cross hostile ground, seize a goal — and return changed. Spectacle serves a core question, not only a map of set pieces.

packs.title: Alternate history
packs.summary: Engine: **point of divergence (POD) + ramifications** — one (or few) historical changes, then a world that follows cause-and-effect from that fork.

packs.title: Biographical historical fiction
packs.summary: Engine: a real figure’s life-arc (or a decisive span) structures the novel; invention fills gaps but must respect documented spine; the drama is constraint of the known + earned speculation.

packs.title: Biopunk
packs.summary: Engine: **bodies, genes, and biotech as control systems** — synthetic biology, black clinics, and uneven enhancement under corporate or state power; flesh as the hackable substrate (cyberpunk’s sibling, not its costume swap).

packs.title: Body horror
packs.summary: Engine: the body becomes unreliable — transformation, invasion, loss of autonomy. Fear of inhabiting changing flesh.

packs.title: Campus / academic novel
packs.summary: Engine: university as closed microcosm — hierarchies, pretension vs appetite, students vs faculty, ideas as status weapons; idiosyncratic characters in unambiguous ranks.

packs.title: Chapter book / early chapter craft
packs.summary: Bridge formats for newly independent readers: short chapters, white space, confidence-building success — between picture books and middle grade.

packs.title: Chick lit (legacy shelf)
packs.summary: Engine: voice-forward contemporary comedy of errors around work, friendship, dating, and self-definition; lighthearted / witty tone; urban(ish) heroine navigating too many choices. Market label largely retired as sexist — craft residue remains useful for comps and tone.

packs.title: Climate fiction (cli-fi)
packs.summary: Engine: **anthropogenic climate pressure as plot weather** — changed or changing climate reshapes daily life, choice, and power; science-grounded speculation, not generic disaster chrome.

packs.title: Comedy / satire fiction
packs.summary: Engine: tonal contract + incongruity. Comic novel wants the laugh to deepen character/stakes; satire wants the laugh to make a truth about power (or a social gap) undeniable.

packs.title: Coming-of-age (adult)
packs.summary: Engine: identity formation after (or beside) the YA shelf — first career, migration, divorce, sobriety, art vocation, late diagnosis; the self re-authored under adult consequences.

packs.title: Conspiracy thriller
packs.summary: Engine: a hidden system (state, corp, cult, cabal) manipulates the visible world; protagonist must prove, survive, or escape the web; paranoia is a feature when earned by pattern, a bug when unmotivated.

packs.title: Contemporary realist fiction
packs.summary: Engine: present-day (or near-present) character drama in a recognizable world; low or no speculative furniture; social and psychological pressure from work, love, money, kinship, health, politics-as-lived.

packs.title: Contemporary romance (CR)
packs.summary: Engine: present-day love under recognizable modern pressure — career, family, phones, money, vulnerability — without supernatural or period scaffolding.

packs.title: Contemporary western / neo-Western
packs.summary: Engine: frontier psychology in a modern West — land, ranch, border, small-city crime, extractive economy; law still thin or compromised; landscape dwarfs human plans.

packs.title: Cosmic / weird horror
packs.summary: Engine: human scale fails against the incomprehensible. Dread from realization and forbidden knowledge — not jump-scare or gore alone.

packs.title: Cozy fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: **comfort, community, and low-to-moderate stakes in a fantastic world** — slice-of-life warmth, found family, craft/food/place love; hope and kindness as the emotional contract (conflict allowed on a dial, not erased).

packs.title: Cozy mystery
packs.summary: Engine: fair-play puzzle + comfort. Reader wants to revisit the town as much as solve the crime.

packs.title: Crime fiction (literary / commercial)
packs.summary: Engine: transgression and its aftermath — caper, heist, underworld, or moral fallout; mystery puzzle optional. Focus is what crime *does* to people and systems, not only who-dunnit.

packs.title: Cyberpunk
packs.summary: Engine: **high tech / low life** — advanced cybernetics, AI, and dataspheres juxtaposed with street-level precarity; megacorps (not nations) as power; identity as editable body/credential.

packs.title: Dark erotica (vs dark romance)
packs.summary: Engine: sexual/moral darkness as the experiential core — discomfort and arousal coexist; romantic HEA is **not** required. Distinct from dark romance, which still owes central love + optimistic couple landing.

packs.title: Dark fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: **horror-tinged fantastic** — dread, the uncanny, or aesthetic terror woven into fantasy formulae; darkness as atmosphere and theme, not only body count.

packs.title: Dark romance
packs.summary: Engine: morally gray / high-heat / taboo-edge courtship that still owes a romance HEA/HFN for most trade readers; darkness pressures the couple.

packs.title: Dieselpunk
packs.summary: Engine: **interwar-to-midcentury diesel / Deco retrofuture** — grease, radio, airpower, and pulp modernity; optimistic “decodence” *or* war-machine pessimism, depending on school.

packs.title: Domestic fiction
packs.summary: Engine: household and kinship stakes — marriage, parenting, eldercare, inheritance, home as stage; the intimate sphere carries the plot. Not the same as domestic thriller (threat/suspense engine).

packs.title: Domestic thriller / intimate psychological suspense
packs.summary: Engine: danger already lives in the house. Threat is intimate — spouse, neighbor, family secret — not a ticking bomb downtown.

packs.title: Dystopian fiction
packs.summary: Engine: **a society worse than ours by design** — oppression, dehumanization, or engineered “perfection” that costs humanity; warning via exaggeration of a present trend.

packs.title: Early reader
packs.summary: Engine: controlled vocabulary + confidence loops — short chapters or spreads that let new readers succeed.

packs.title: Epic / high fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: **secondary world + scale** — invented setting with stakes that threaten nations, peoples, or the world’s order; wonder paid for with consistency.

packs.title: Erotic romance
packs.summary: Engine: **romance HEA/HFN + sex as load-bearing growth** — remove the sexual journey and the love story collapses; keep the optimistic couple ending and you are still *romance*, not erotica.

packs.title: Erotica (genre engine)
packs.summary: Sexual journey as the story’s core — not “romance with more sex.” Style bans / anatomy realism → . Scene function, heat contracts, consent → . Romance HEA engine → . Erotic romance → . Subgenres → .

packs.title: Age-gap erotica (adult–adult only)
packs.summary: Engine: **experience, life-stage, and power asymmetry between consenting adults** as erotic and emotional fuel — not a “mentor the young” illegal frame.

packs.title: BDSM / kink erotica (incl. D/s)
packs.summary: Engine: **negotiated power exchange as the story’s trust ladder** — dominance/submission, bondage, discipline, sadomasochism, or other kink as the sexual journey’s spine. Market often files under erotica *or* erotic romance; structure (HEA?) decides.

packs.title: Billionaire / workplace-power erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **institutional or wealth asymmetry as erotic fuel** — boss/employee, owner/talent, rich/poor logistics — among **consenting adults**. The job or money must change who can say no, who is watched, and what exposure costs.

packs.title: Contemporary erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **present-day desire under recognizable modern pressure** — phones, work, apps, reputation, housing — with sexual journey as spine (erotica) or load-bearing path to HEA (erotic romance).

packs.title: Fantasy erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **secondary-world or magic-system constraints on desire** — courts, curses, magical binding, nonhuman customs — with sexual journey primary (erotica) or HEA+sex load-bearing (erotic romance / romantasy-heat).

packs.title: F/F erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **female–female desire as the sexual center** — gaze, pacing, and power must be written for that pairing, not as mirrored M/F with pronouns swapped.

packs.title: Forbidden / taboo-as-market-label erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **desire that violates a social, professional, or communal boundary among consenting adults** — the forbiddenness is the heat source *and* the plot pressure.

packs.title: Historical erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **period-constrained desire** — privacy, reputation, law, class, contraception, clothing logistics — with sexual journey as spine. Research is load-bearing; anachronistic sexual ethics need intentional framing.

packs.title: Literary / transgressive erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **arousal braided with language, theme, or social critique** — the sexual journey still primary, but prose ambition and idea-pressure distinguish it from commercial heat-first erotica.

packs.title: Ménage / poly erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **multi-partner desire where ethics, logistics, and group chemistry are the plot** — not “extra body in the bed” decoration.

packs.title: M/F erotica (unmarked default)
packs.summary: Engine: **male–female sexual journey** — the culturally “default” pairing, which means **heterosexual scripts hide inside craft choices**. Make those choices conscious.

packs.title: M/M erotica
packs.summary: Engine: male–male desire as the sexual (and often emotional) center — not “het erotica with genders swapped.” Community reading conventions, body logistics, and voice matter.

packs.title: Monster / creature erotica (consenting-adult shelf)
packs.summary: Engine: erotic charge from genuine otherness — nonhuman body, instinct, culture — while keeping adult agency and chosen desire.

packs.title: Paranormal erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **supernatural rules that change desire, body, or bonding** — hunger, heat cycles, glamour, immortality — while sexual journey (erotica) or love+sex (erotic romance) stays central. Distinct from urban fantasy’s case/quest-first promise.

packs.title: Reverse harem / why-choose (erotica ↔ erotic romance)
packs.summary: Engine: **one protagonist builds lasting romantic/sexual bonds with multiple partners and does not “pick one”** — group resolution is the point. Market-dominant home is **romance / erotic romance**; pure erotica versions exist but readers often expect HEA-shaped landings.

packs.title: Sci-fi erotica
packs.summary: Engine: **a novum that changes bodies, reproduction, privacy, or sexual culture** — tech, aliens, space logistics — with sexual journey as spine. If the love story + HEA dominates, you’re in SF romance; if the case/novum dominates without sex-spine, plain SF.

packs.title: Short-form erotica (shorts, anthologies, serials)
packs.summary: Engine: **compressed sexual journey with complete episode payoff** — heat density high; unity via theme, character change, or series hook rather than sprawling subplot.

packs.title: Experimental / postmodern fiction
packs.summary: Engine: form as argument — structure, typography, metafiction, fragmentation, or rule-games carry meaning; the book teaches you how to read it; realism is optional and often sabotaged on purpose.

packs.title: Fairy-tale / mythic retelling
packs.summary: Engine: recognizable source machinery + deliberate innovation angle. Reader hears the old story under the new one; standalone completeness still required.

packs.title: Multi-generational family saga
packs.summary: Engine: dynasty time-scale — inheritance of conflict, property, secrets, and temperament across generations; history enters through the family doorway; no single protagonist owns the whole meaning.

packs.title: Fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: the world and its rules (especially magic) — wonder paid for with consistency.

packs.title: Farce (novel / comic mode)
packs.summary: Engine: escalating misunderstanding as a timing machine; implausible but rule-bound situations; physical and social doors slamming; speed toward collapse/reveal.

packs.title: First contact
packs.summary: Engine: encounter with the alien other — detection, communication, ethics, and consequence when sapient species meet; the novum is the otherness and the interface, not only the spaceship.

packs.title: Folk horror
packs.summary: Engine: rural / isolated community + folklore or ritual pressure; landscape and social complicity scare more than jump-scare monsters.

packs.title: Gaslamp fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: Victorian / Edwardian (or analogous) aesthetic + unexplained supernatural — manners and lamp-lit society pressure a magic/uncanny plot.

packs.title: Generation ship
packs.summary: Engine: closed society under multi-generational voyage pressure — the ship is world; original passengers die en route; descendants inherit a mission they did not choose.

packs.title: Ghost story
packs.summary: Engine: unfinished business made present. Haunting as pressure — malevolence, grief, or both — arriving by crescendo into ordinary life.

packs.title: Gothic fiction
packs.summary: Engine: **atmosphere + buried secret + uncanny**. Unsettles; does not require visceral scare. Setting is not backdrop — it is pressure.

packs.title: Grimdark
packs.summary: Engine: agency under rotten systems — morally gray people forced to choose in a world where right action is costly, compromised, or seemingly futile; darkness with argument, not wallpaper.

packs.title: Hard science fiction
packs.summary: Engine: **science/engineering constraint as plot pressure** — known or carefully extrapolated science is the backbone; problems solvable (or tragically insoluble) *within* those rules; enabling miracles minimized or paid for.

packs.title: Historical fiction craft
packs.summary: Past lived as present. Research supports drama; drama isn’t a museum tour.

packs.title: Historical adventure
packs.summary: Engine: travel, empire, survival, or quest inside a researched past; ordeal geography + period constraint; competence under pressure with historical teeth (disease, distance, politics).

packs.title: Historical mystery
packs.summary: Engine: period constraint + fair-play (or procedural) investigation; the past’s tech, law, and manners shape what can be known and how; dual pleasure of puzzle and time-travel texture.

packs.title: Historical romance (HR)
packs.summary: Engine: period constraint as courtship pressure — manners, law, class, reputation, travel speed, and marriage-as-contract force couple choices; research is part of the promise.

packs.title: Horror fiction
packs.summary: Engine: dread, not gore. Reader should feel unsafe.

packs.title: Horror-comedy
packs.summary: Engine: tension → release toggles between dread and laugh. Both engines must work — comedy in a monster costume is not enough.

packs.title: Legal thriller
packs.summary: Engine: strategy inside a recognized process. High stakes + rules (or the hiding of broken rules). Not a gunfight — a chess match with liberty, reputation, or life on the line.

packs.title: LGBTQ+ romance
packs.summary: Engine: same HEA/HFN romance contract with identity, community, and/or disclosure stakes that vary by submarket; pairing is not a pronoun swap on a default straight template.

packs.title: LitRPG & progression fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: measurable advancement as plot — power, skills, and understanding rise in ways the reader can track; in LitRPG the visible system UI is part of the reading experience.

packs.title: Locked-room / impossible crime
packs.summary: Engine: the crime appears physically impossible; the spectacle is logic. Reader wants the “how” as much as the “who.”

packs.title: Lost-world / expedition
packs.summary: Engine: discovery of a hidden place (valley, plateau, city, pocket ecosystem) + isolation; wonder and threat braid; getting in is plot, getting out is character.

packs.title: Low fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: fantastic intrusion into a recognizable (or realist-scoped) world — magic is rare, disruptive, or psychologically ambiguous; “low” names familiarity of the world, not quality.

packs.title: Magical realism
packs.summary: Engine: one (or few) impossibilities inside a fully intact ordinary world, narrated without apology. Seam craft: magic enters without tearing the real.

packs.title: Medical thriller
packs.summary: Engine: body, hospital, research lab, or public-health system as threat stage; specialized knowledge creates asymmetric power; conspiracy or malpractice often braids with a ticking clinical clock.

packs.title: Middle grade craft
packs.summary: Fiction for ~8–12 (core often 9–12): wonder, friendship/family engines, kid agency, hope — not teen YA shelved young.

packs.title: Military science fiction
packs.summary: Engine: **doctrine, unit, and the tech of war in a speculative setting** — protagonists usually inside a military (or mercenary) organization; conflict described with attention to tactics, weapons, logistics, and the soldier’s lived difference from civilian life.

packs.title: Mystery / crime
packs.summary: Engine: the puzzle. Reader plays along.

packs.title: Mythic fantasy / mythic fiction
packs.summary: Engine: gods, folklore patterns, and living myth as system — tropes of legend operate with felt inevitability or ritual logic; stories rewrite, inhabit, or punk the old patterns rather than only tour a secondary-world magic system.

packs.title: Near-future / mundane SF
packs.summary: Engine: tomorrow’s tech and systems in a recognizable world — extrapolation from present science and society; usually Earth or Solar System; restraint about FTL, galactic empires, and easy aliens so estrangement hits closer to home.

packs.title: New Adult (genre engine)
packs.summary: Protagonists roughly **18–29** navigating first independence — older-YA emotional immediacy with adult agency and (often) adult heat. Category never fully stabilized in Big Five shelving; craft still useful for voice, stakes, and comps.

packs.title: Noir / hardboiled / crime fiction
packs.summary: Engine: moral compromise in a rigged world. Solving the case is secondary to what the case costs the protagonist.

packs.title: Occult / demonic horror
packs.summary: Engine: ritual, forbidden practice, and entities that answer. Faith, will, and knowledge as weapons — and as liabilities.

packs.title: Paranormal romance (PNR)
packs.summary: Engine: supernatural rules that complicate courtship — immortality, mating bonds, secrecy, predator nature — while central love + HEA/HFN still win.

packs.title: PI / lone detective
packs.summary: Engine: a private investigator (or functional loner) works a case outside institutional power — personal code vs corrupt world. Case + cost to the sleuth.

packs.title: Picture book craft
packs.summary: Format-first kidlit: ~32 pages, read-aloud performance, words leave room for art. Not “a short story with pictures.”

packs.title: Pirate / nautical adventure
packs.summary: Engine: ship as society; sea as engine (weather, navigation, scarcity); command, mutiny, prize, and code under pressure; horizontal world of decks and vertical world of rank.

packs.title: Police procedural
packs.summary: Engine: investigation as **system work** — team, protocol, error, paperwork, and the gap between what TV promises and what jurisdictions allow.

packs.title: Portal fantasy & isekai
packs.summary: Engine: **crossing a threshold into another world’s rules** — adaptation, competence, and transformation under a new physics/society; the portal (or death/summon/rebirth) is the catalytic novum, not the whole story.

packs.title: Psychological thriller
packs.summary: Engine: thrills from mind games, unstable perception, and eroded trust more than spectacle; action is often suppressed; dread lives in what characters believe — and whether the reader should.

packs.title: Regency romance
packs.summary: Engine: Austen-adjacent manners market — Season, reputation, marriage mart, and wit as courtship weapons; period constraint is the romance obstacle course.

packs.title: Romance (genre engine)
packs.summary: Market promise: a central love story + emotionally satisfying optimistic ending. Couple beats → . Heat scene craft → . Erotica (distinct) → . Erotic romance → .

packs.title: Romantasy / fantasy romance
packs.summary: Engine: fantasy machinery + romance machinery both load-bearing — magic, courts, quests pressure trust/power/belonging; yearning pressures the plot. Labels disagree; position by primary promise.

packs.title: Romantic comedy (novel)
packs.summary: Engine: meet-cute → comic obstacles → earned HEA — humor is load-bearing, not garnish; the laugh engine and the romance engine must share the same plot spine.

packs.title: Romantic suspense
packs.summary: Engine: dual engines — intrigue/crime/threat *and* courtship — each raising the other’s stakes until mystery resolves **and** the relationship solidifies (HEA/HFN required).

packs.title: Science fiction
packs.summary: Engine: the **novum** — the new thing / “what if?”

packs.title: Science fiction / futuristic romance
packs.summary: Engine: novum complicates intimacy — other worlds, futures, alien biology, or tech regimes change loyalty, body, law, or distance — while romance HEA/HFN remains the emotional payoff.

packs.title: Slasher / survival horror
packs.summary: Engine: predatory pursuit. Body count vs survivor agency. The threat is (or was) human — walks among us.

packs.title: Slice-of-life / quiet novel
packs.summary: Engine: texture and character over plot machinery; meaning accumulates through ordinary days.

packs.title: Slipstream
packs.summary: Engine: cognitive dissonance / “fiction of strangeness” — genre furniture and literary technique bleed; the familiar made strange (or reverse) without full SF/F market contract.

packs.title: Small-town / community romance
packs.summary: Engine: ensemble town pressure + central love story — gossip, history, and overlapping relationships force the couple’s choices.

packs.title: Soft / sociological science fiction
packs.summary: Engine: **culture, language, psyche, and institutions as the novum** — soft sciences (or human emotional consequence) foregrounded; physics may be lighter or handwaved so the thought experiment can stay on people and systems.

packs.title: Solarpunk
packs.summary: Engine: **solutions taken to radical conclusion** — sustainable, community-scaled futures (renewables, mutual aid, ecological repair) imagined as achievable; optimism without denying crisis.

packs.title: Space opera
packs.summary: Engine: **epic scale in space** — FTL (or equivalent), large stakes (war, empire, civilization), adventure and character drama against a vast backdrop; wonder + momentum more than lab rigor (unless “new space opera” hybrid).

packs.title: Sports romance
packs.summary: Engine: athlete / team / public-performance milieu pressures the central love story; remove the game and the romance should weaken.

packs.title: Spy / espionage fiction
packs.summary: Engine: secrecy, tradecraft-as-behavior, betrayal, institutional friction. Tension from what is known, denied, and compromised — not primarily from open force.

packs.title: Steampunk
packs.summary: Engine: **retrofuturist steam-age tech as argument** — anachronistic steam / clockwork inventions reshape society; Victorian (or analogous industrial) aesthetics serve a question about progress, power, and who pays.

packs.title: Survival adventure
packs.summary: Engine: environment as antagonist; skills, luck, and will under scarcity; the plot is staying alive long enough for a harder choice to appear.

packs.title: Sword & sorcery
packs.summary: Engine: **personal-scale adventure with pulp velocity** — sword-wielding (anti)heroes in invented or legendary milieux where magic works; situational conflicts and survival/gain more than world-saving good-vs-evil crusades.

packs.title: Techno-thriller
packs.summary: Engine: **plausible near-future (or present) technology as the stakes machine** — thriller pacing + exceptional technical specificity; the plot turns on *how the tech actually works*.

packs.title: Thriller / suspense
packs.summary: Engine: pacing + escalating stakes; reader feels the clock. Mood = apprehension, anticipation, anxiety — if it doesn’t thrill, it isn’t doing the job.

packs.title: Time travel
packs.summary: Engine: **cost and logic of moving in time** — paradox, predestination, alternate timelines, or tourist/war uses of the past/future; the mechanism’s rules are the novum that generates plot.

packs.title: True-crime novelization / faction
packs.summary: Engine: a real case (or tightly researched real milieu) scaffolds a narrative; drama shapes truth without inventing harm carelessly; ethics of naming and invention are load-bearing, not afterthought.

packs.title: Upmarket / book-club fiction
packs.summary: Engine: page-turning plot + carefully crafted prose + discussable dilemma. Trade/publishing positioning more than a bookstore shelf label — writers use it for query/comp promises.

packs.title: Upper middle grade (upper MG)
packs.summary: Engine: older MG voice with slightly sharper stakes — still kid agency and hope-forward, closer to teen complexity without full YA autonomy/heat contracts.

packs.title: Urban fantasy
packs.summary: Engine: **familiar city + secret (or newly visible) supernatural** — friction between rent, phones, and the uncanny.

packs.title: Utopia / ambiguous utopia
packs.summary: Engine: ideal (or would-be ideal) society under stress-test — the thought experiment is the social design; plot proves what the utopia costs, whom it excludes, or how it holds when desire and difference appear.

packs.title: War fiction / military / wartime historical
packs.summary: Engine: organized violence and its human systems — combat unit, command, home front, occupation, aftermath; loyalty, fear, moral injury, and mission pressure; period accuracy serves lived cost, not only hardware.

packs.title: Western
packs.summary: Engine: landscape shapes character; law vs freedom at the edge of civilization. Cost of order measured in what gets destroyed along the way.

packs.title: Women’s fiction (genre engine)
packs.summary: Driving force: the protagonist’s emotional journey toward a more fulfilled self — not “any book by/for women,” and not automatic romance.

packs.title: YA / coming-of-age craft
packs.summary: Category defined by protagonist age + narrative stance for teen emotional experience — not “any book with a teenager.”

packs.title: YA genre hybrids (romance / fantasy / SF / thriller)
packs.summary: Engine: YA age-band contract + an adult genre engine — voice/agency/stakes of YA stay primary; the co-engine still pays its obligatory moments.

packs.title: ElevenLabs Music
packs.summary: UI prompt plus lyrics, or composition-plan text blocks. Write the song first; this kit only formats ElevenLabs paste. No SDK samples.

packs.title: Song lyrics
packs.summary: Singable lyrics for a brief — one promise, chorus first, palettes as opt-in modules. Host kits wrap tags after the song exists.

packs.title: Mureka
packs.summary: Lyrics-first wrap — structure tags in the lyrics, style in the prompt field. Write the song first; this kit only formats Mureka paste.

packs.title: Seedance 2.0 video prompts
packs.summary: Chapter-draft craft for Seedance 2.0 visual prompts — camera, staging, continuity (~15s), refs.

packs.title: Seedance 2.5 video prompts
packs.summary: Chapter-draft craft for Seedance 2.5 visual prompts — camera, staging, continuity (~30s), refs.

packs.title: Suno
packs.summary: Custom Mode wrap — style field (no brackets) plus lyrics tags. Write the song first; this kit only formats Suno paste.

packs.title: Udio
packs.summary: Guidance-tag wrap — topic plus comma-separated genres, then official lyrics tags. Write the song first; this kit only formats Udio paste.
